MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  SEPTEMBER 10, 2024

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

MAYOR SCHMITZ called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Led by MAYOR SCHMITZ.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan

City Council Members Absent:  Brown Schachter

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Attorney Steve McEwen
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Community Development Director Jeannie Naughton
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit
  Assistant to the City Manager Jessica Slawson

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  PROCLAMATION: DECLARING SEPTEMBER 2024 "NATIONAL PREPAREDNESS
  MONTH"

MAYOR SCHMITZ presented a proclamation declaring September 2024 as “National
Preparedness Month.”

B.  PROCLAMATION: DECLARING SEPTEMBER 15 – OCTOBER 15 "HISPANIC
  HERITAGE MONTH"

MAYOR SCHMITZ presented a proclamation September 15 – October 15, 2024 as
“Hispanic Heritage Month.”

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority consent of the City
Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member prior to the
roll call vote. (Items removed will be considered under New Business.)

  MAYOR PRO TEM STEGURA moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF, TO
  APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS 5A-E, G-L AS FOLLOWS BY THE
  FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan

None.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
SEPTEMBER 10, 2024
 8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  USER FEE UPDATE - COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT AND PUBLIC WORKS
  DEPARTMENTS

  Recommendation: That the City Council receive the report on the comprehensive
  User Fee Study for the Community Development and Public Works Departments,
  discuss the issues, and direct staff to return at the next regularly scheduled meeting
  with a draft cost recovery policy and annual increase mechanism, for City Council
  consideration.

Community Development Director Naughton provided a staff report (as per the agenda
material).

Khushboo Ingle, Vice President of Matrix Consulting Group, and Madison Dixson, Senior
Consultant, provided a presentation of the User Fee Study, including the background, study
objectives, methodology, and the fee study results.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF confirmed that the Los Angeles County fee schedule that was
followed previously was regularly adjusted.

Consultant Ingle explained that an overarching goal of recovering 100% can be set, in
response to MAYOR PRO TEM STEGURA.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM
  STEGURA, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  DIRECT STAFF TO RETURN AT THE NEXT REGULARLY SCHEDULED
  MEETING WITH A DRAFT COST RECOVERY POLICY AND ANNUAL
  INCREASE MECHANISM, FOR CITY COUNCIL CONSIDERATION.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  Brown Schachter

B.  APPROVAL OF THE GOOD NEIGHBOR PLEDGE THROUGH THE SOUTH BAY
  CITIES COUNCIL OF GOVERNMENTS IN RESPONSE TO JOHNSON V. GRANTS
  PASS SUPREME COURT RULING

  Recommendation: That the City Council authorize the Mayor to sign the Good
  Neighbor Pledge.

Assistant to the City Manager Slawson provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF thanked Ronson Chu, South Bay Cities Council of Governments
(SBCCOG) Senior Project Manager, Homeless Services, for attending.

MAYOR PRO TEM STEGURA thanked Ronson Chu for being at this meeting, and thinks this
pledge memorializes the approach that SBCCOG and other cities have already taken to be
compassionate and helpful to those that are unhoused.

MAYOR SCHMITZ also thanked Mr. Chu for his attendance and work on this issue.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
Mr. Chu made a few comments about the Good Neighbor Pledge.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN stated that the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department
unit that works on homeless issues has not made one arrest and works with a great deal of
compassion.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
SEPTEMBER 10, 2024
   MAYOR PRO TEM STEGURA moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF, TO
  APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AUTHORIZE THE MAYOR TO SIGN THE GOOD NEIGHBOR PLEDGE.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  Brown Schachter

9.  OLD BUSINESS

None.

10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

None.

11.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF attended the South Bay Cities Council of Governments
(SBCCOG) Steering Committee meeting yesterday.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN attended the California Contract Cities Association’s
(CCCA) Fall Educational Summit.

MAYOR PRO TEM STEGURA attended the Clean Power Alliance (CPA) monthly board
meeting.

MAYOR SCHMITZ noted there will be a September Los Angeles County Sanitation Districts
Board Meeting and a Regional Meeting in October.

MAYOR SCHMITZ also attended the monthly Peninsula Mayors’ meeting.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN brought up the recent burglaries in the commercial district,
and City Manager Grammer stated that staff would be meeting with the Lomita Station
Captain to discuss the incidents and what can be done to support the businesses.

12.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS

MAYOR SCHMITZ announced the City Celebration event this Saturday, September 14, 2024.

13.  CLOSED SESSION

A.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL - ANTICIPATED LITIGATION
  Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(2)
  Significant exposure to litigation: one potential case

  NO REPORTABLE ACTION.
14.  ADJOURNMENT

At 7:55 p.m. MAYOR SCHMITZ adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, September 24, 2024 at
7:00 p.m. for the purpose of a Regular meeting.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Lauren Pettit, City Clerk  Velveth Schmitz, Mayor

SEPTEMBER 10, 2024
